title: Compact trace mode + annotation search — grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact-density trace viewer mode coupled with an annotation / span-text search and small interaction details we want to scope for the next sprint. The goal: let engineers scan large traces (>>100 spans) quickly, find spans by text/annotation, and temporarily expand interesting chains without losing the global time context. Not a finished spec — heavily opinionated notes and grooming checklist.

Problem statement / context:
- Production traces can be very wide and deep; the standard waterfall with full span rows is too tall for fast triage.
- Current trace UI forces a lot of vertical scrolling and loses sight of sibling spans/time relationships.
- Common user flows: "find the first occurrence of a backend error", "see latency distribution across services for this trace", "pin a handful of spans for deeper inspection and share snapshot".
- We need a compact representation that preserves relative timing, searchable annotations, and lightweight expand-on-demand interactions.

Key UX concepts (high level):
1) Compact rows (baseline):
   - Row height ~ 28px (vs 48px current).
   - Condense metadata: service + operation in one pill; hide heavy fields by default (attrs, logs).
   - Show a micro-waterfall sparkline to the right of the pill for per-row timing (start/duration scaled to trace width).

2) Mini-ruler & global context:
   - Horizontal time ruler at top always visible.
   - When a row is expanded, show a translucent overlay that preserves siblings (no reflow of other rows).
   - Sticky time cursor on hover to compare spans quickly.

3) Annotation / span-text search:
   - Unified search bar above trace list. Default typeahead matches: span.name, service, tag keys/values, log message text.
   - Support exact-match, contains, and regex toggles. Example presets: "error:true", "http.status_code=504", "+db -cache" (AND/NOT short syntax).
   - Search results highlight matched terms in compact pill and also show a count (+N) when collapsed.

4) Fold / group heuristics:
   - Auto-group very short sibling spans (<5ms or <2% of parent) into a single folded node with an aggregated duration and count badge.
   - Provide an affordance to expand folded group inline (chevron) to reveal original spans without changing scroll position.

5) Pinning and temporal bookmarks:
   - Right-click "Pin span" or keyboard 'p' to pin. Pinned spans get a narrow left rail indicator and persist across view changes.
   - Temporal bookmarks: user can mark a time window range (drag on ruler) and save as a named bookmark for sharing.

6) Quick actions and context menu:
   - Right-click on a compact pill: expand, copy span id, pin, create alert (opens rules modal), jump to logs (if linked).
   - Double-click opens full detail pane (right-side drawer) with logs/attrs/children.

7) Keyboard navigation & accessibility:
   - Arrow keys to move selection across visible rows. Enter to expand selected span; Shift+Enter to expand full chain; / to focus search.
   - Focus ring and screen-reader labels for compact pills. Ensure contrast for condensed text.

8) Snapshot share + lightweight export:
   - When user selects N spans (via shift-click or pins), allow "Create snapshot" which packages those spans and a small set of metadata into a permalink that can be pasted in Slack.
   - Snapshot respects pinned spans and any active filters. Option to redact PII toggled in modal.

Sketches (rough wireframes):
   - Top area: toolbar with back, trace-id, small-time-ruler, search box, density toggle (Compact / Comfortable / Expanded).
   - Left column: minimal checkboxes + service color strip + pinned indicator (narrow).
   - Middle: compact pill with service.op pill, small op icon, matched term highlight, folded-group badge, micro-waterfall line (thin).
   - Right: micro-metrics: duration, start offset, error badge. Small chevron to expand in-place.

Interaction flows (examples):
Flow A: Find-first-error -> pin -> snapshot
  1. User types "error:true" in search and sees 3 hits across the trace; pills with red highlights and counts.
  2. User presses 'n' to jump to next match; selected row scrolls into view and is briefly flashed.
  3. Right-click -> Pin span. Repeat for 2 more spans.
  4. Click "Create snapshot" -> modal shows pinned spans and generates a short permalink. Option: include full trace or only selected spans.

Flow B: Investigate noisy short spans
  1. User toggles "fold tiny spans" (auto on in compact mode).
  2. See folded group badges with counts and aggregated duration; click to expand inline — newly revealed spans animate open with preserved ruler context.
  3. Select one child span and press Enter to open detail drawer.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets):
  - RED-4387: compact-density layout implementation (skeleton + density toggle) — 5 pts — P0
    acceptance_criteria: ["density toggle exists", "rows render at ~28px height in compact", "micro-waterfall aligns to global ruler"]
  - RED-4412: annotation / span-text search with regex and boolean short-syntax — 8 pts — P0
    acceptance_criteria: ["typeahead across name/service/tags/logs", "regex toggle works", "keyboard / focuses search"]
  - RED-4440: folding heuristics (threshold + UI) — 3 pts — P1
    acceptance_criteria: ["folded groups show count and aggregated duration", "inline expand preserves scroll and time alignment"]
  - RED-4499: pinning, snapshot permalink export — 5 pts — P1
    acceptance_criteria: ["pins persist while browsing", "snapshot link includes pinned spans and preserves filters"]
  - RED-4522: keyboard nav, screen reader labels, contrast tests — 3 pts — P1

Open questions / risks:
  - Data size: searching logs within large traces can be expensive. Do we require an index or only search attached logs on-demand? Proposal: initial version matches only span attributes and short log previews; full-text logs search as an async job.
  - Backend surface: need endpoints for folded-group expansion that return original spans without re-fetching full trace. Cache considerations for private deployments.
  - Snapshots and privacy: define default redaction level for snapshots for external sharing. Legal to weigh in.
  - Performance on Dedicated/Private: ensure compact rendering does not cause massive DOM churn for traces with thousands of spans. Consider virtualization (windowing).

Metrics / success criteria:
  - Time-to-first-match: median time for users to find first matching span reduced by 40% in compact mode vs current UI.
  - Number of vertical scroll events per trace session reduced by 50% for traces >200 spans.
  - Usage: X% of trace viewers toggle compact mode within 1 week of feature launch (instrument).

Design/implementation notes for engineers:
  - Frontend: React component tree should separate visual row from data row to allow inline expansion without reflow.
  - Rendering: use canvas or lightweight SVG for micro-waterfalls to avoid many positioned divs when traces are huge. Build a small renderer shared with timeline sparklines.
  - Accessibility: all compact pills must have an accessible name of the form "service operation duration start-offset status".
  - Events: telemetry for search queries, pin actions, expand/fold counts, snapshot creation. Prefix events with trace.v2.compact.*

Next steps / owners:
  - UX: Ivy — finalize wireframes and hi-fi mocks for compact and expanded interactions (due 2026-03-08).
  - Eng FE: Rohan — prototype compact row renderer and micro-waterfall canvas (spike 2 days).
  - Eng BE: Maya — scope search index requirements and folded-group expansion APIs (sync with infra).
  - Legal/Security: request guidance on snapshot redaction (Evan).

Notes to reviewers:
  - Please add comments inline with sample gif sketches or short Looms showing painful traces from support. I added two quick links in linked_artifacts to start.
  - If we decide the fold threshold should be user-configurable, add a small global preference under Trace settings rather than in the toolbar.

-- end --
